lines.speaker: d
lines.text: November fourteenth, two thousand four. Off southern California, four Navy flyers are sent to check something strange.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: For a week, radar on the U.S.S. Princeton had tracked objects that operators said dropped from eighty thousand feet in seconds.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Commander David Frayvor and Lootenant Commander Alex Deetrich, each with a backseat officer, find whitewater churning over the ocean.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Above it hovers a small white object. Forty feet long. No wings. No exhaust.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Frayvor spirals down to look. The object turns, and mirrors him, rising to meet his jet.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Then it leaves. Another jet films it on infrared. The Pentagon released that video in twenty twenty, calling it unidentified.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Skeptics point to glare, parallax, even sensor errors.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Four trained flyers watched it for five minutes.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Misread sensors, or something that mirrored a fighter jet?
